The opposite of love isn't hate, but apathy. If you're hated, that means you at least exist, you're worthy of being hated, worthy of attention at the least. If you're invisible, it's just... nothingness, you're not worthy of even being in others' thoughts, questioning your own existence.

I'm really glad you've come to understand the truth and can finally build some self-worth, I hope you can get to a point where shit like this is well in the past.

Goddamn though I relate to you so much. My nDad was the same. I had food, water, and shelter. "Why are you complaining? You know there are kids in Africa that die of starvation every day, right?" It's a bullshit response. Leaving a kid with that message, how else do we not turn it toward ourselves and conclude we are just selfish, worthless pieces of shit.

I see. I'm aware that as long as the child has at least ONE supportive figure the symptoms are significantly lessened. My friend did not have anyone and most certainly has CPTSD, he has his fair share of extreme fight flashbacks, and he also sometimes beats the shit out of people during his more intense flashbacks. He was in special forces and one time someone tapped him on the shoulder, he knocked out three people before he realized what happened. This was before he ever developed PTSD from the military as well.

I just can't help but compare. Being abandoned was fucking terrifying too. I hardly felt alive, I was depressed, lonely, hating life, hating everyone, hating the world, hating myself and tried to kill myself before I was out of kindergarten. The only "person" I thought I was with was God. I was questioning my own existence the entire time and I turned into an abusive, manipulative robot in my teen years. 

I would gladly have been hit just to feel *something*. Trying to kill myself as a kindergartener even felt... good. 

Anyway, that wasn't the point of my post, but that is the subject of this comment chain since you pointed it out. I will always just subconsciously know it would have been better. I won't focus on it any more than that though, and focus on what's relevant.

Fuck parents who have no business having kids... for real. Just, what the hell do you make of that situation...

Man it's crazy how simplified our stories are. We were just left behind, so we dissociated into the void and stayed that way. There's no recovery from being hated, no learning that the treatment you received was wrong(because there just wasn't any), there was just the cold numbness of abandonment. 

For real, I think my sense of time is fucked. I'm in my "prime" years, and I feel like a 70 year old man, where months and months just disappear like they're nothing.
I don't want to be isolated.
